name: One Last Wish
label: Dischord
lede: Six shows in four months, twelve songs on one tape at Inner Ear, and a record Dischord sat on for thirteen years because it didn't want to be the label of dead bands.

eras.title: The house on Garfield Street
eras.text: Revolution Summer changed how D.C. punk sounded, and it also changed how it lived: group houses became the scene's living rooms. The Garfield Street house in the Cathedral neighborhood started in 1985 with Rites of Spring's Brendan Canty and Guy Picciotto and Embrace's Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson under one roof. By early 1986 both bands were finished, after a dozen or so shows apiece.

years.h: Rites of Spring and Embrace share the Garfield Street house
years.p: [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] and [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] of [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] move into the Garfield Street house near the National Cathedral with [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] and [[Ivor Hanson|a17981f7-ab3d-46dc-859a-582ac894cb20]] of [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]].
years.xp: Dischord calls the group house a centerpiece of the D.C. underground for years to come.

years.h: Embrace play their last show; Rites of Spring already gone
years.p: Embrace plays its final show at the 9:30 Club with [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]], after Rites of Spring has already split. The Garfield Street roommates are free.

years.h: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986
yt: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986

eras.title: Four months, six shows
eras.text: Michael Hampton, a guitarist who had come up through SOA, Faith and Embrace, joined three-quarters of Rites of Spring. Dischord says One Last Wish was even more short-lived than the two bands it came from: six shows in the four months it was together, and one studio session.

years.h: One Last Wish: Michael Hampton and three-quarters of Rites of Spring
years.p: Guy Picciotto on vocals and guitar, [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] on bass, Brendan Canty on drums, and Michael Hampton on guitar and vocals. The only Rites of Spring member missing is bassist Mike Fellows.
years.xp: Dischord puts the start right after Rites of Spring and Embrace split in early 1986. Wikipedia dates the formation to May 1986. Either way, the band was built by roommates and old friends: Janney had played guitar next to Hampton in [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]], and Canty, Picciotto and Janney had just come out of Rites of Spring together, with Janney switching from guitar to bass.

years.h: One Last Wish play their first shows, mostly benefits
years.p: According to Wikipedia, One Last Wish start playing shows in August, mostly D.C. benefits. Dischord counts six shows in all.

eras.title: Shelved, then one song slips out
eras.text: One Last Wish dissolved, its members kept playing together as Happy Go Licky and in Fugazi, and the band's Inner Ear tape stayed in a drawer. Dischord said why: it didn't want more posthumous releases.

years.p: Wikipedia and Punktastic date One Last Wish's split to January 1987. Dischord gives no month, only that the November 1986 Inner Ear session was the band's last activity.

years.h: One Last Wish members form Happy Go Licky and join Fugazi
years.p: Guy Picciotto, Eddie Janney and Brendan Canty reunite with Mike Fellows as [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]]. Canty drums for [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] from its first show that September, and Picciotto is soon singing with them too.

years.h: One Last Wish's Burning in the Undertow on State of the Union
years.p: One song from One Last Wish's 1986 Inner Ear session lands on Dischord's benefit compilation State of the Union. Dischord says it only increased the interest in the rest of the tape.

eras.title: Named for the only year it lived
eras.text: Ten years after the compilation track, the whole One Last Wish session finally came out as 1986, titled for the year the band existed. It has only grown in stature since.

years.h: 1986: One Last Wish's shelved album, 13 years late
years.p: One Last Wish recorded twelve songs at Inner Ear in November 1986, and Dischord shelved them, wary of more records by defunct bands. They came out in 1999 as Dischord No. 118, co-released with Guy Picciotto's Peterbilt label.
years.xp:
[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produced and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] engineered the session, which covers the whole songbook: Hide, Break to Broken, My Better Half, Loss Like a Seed, Three Unkind Silences and Home Is the Place. By the time the tape was finished, the band was essentially over.

Wikipedia and Punktastic both say Dischord didn't want to be seen as a label of defunct bands, and One Last Wish already was one. Burning in the Undertow slipped out on State of the Union in 1989; the rest waited a decade, titled for the year the band existed.

years.h: One Last Wish on 20 Years of Dischord
years.p: One Last Wish gets a place on the label's anniversary box set, next to Rites of Spring and Embrace, the bands it came out of.

years.h: Vulture ranks One Last Wish's My Better Half No. 81
years.p: Vulture's list of the 100 greatest emo songs includes My Better Half, from One Last Wish, a band that played six shows.
